conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit words written through the transmit path and serialized on the LED output; the LED operation depends on these words.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The payload is exposed as the serialized neoled_o waveform at lines 266, 270 and 282, so an integrator may need to restrict disclosure. conceptual assets.information: The stored enable setting that activates the LED engine, drives the clock-generator enable, and controls whether queued transmission data is retained; the peripheral depends on it to operate.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: A bus write stores the enable setting at line 130, and it directly controls clkgen_en_o at line 160 and engine state at line 231, so unauthorized modification can change the operating behavior. The setting clears the transmit FIFO at line 193 and gates engine operation at line 231, so changing it can block or discard required transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could rewrite the enable setting to stop the engine, clear queued data or assert the clock-generator enable at an unintended time.

conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could rewrite the format settings so transmitted words use the wrong bit length or strobe sequence.

conceptual assets.information: The stored prescaler and total, zero-bit-high and one-bit-high timing settings that define the LED waveform rate and pulse widths; the peripheral depends on them to generate a valid serial waveform.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt event generated from the enabled transmit engine and FIFO occupancy conditions; interrupt-driven software may depend on it to service or refill transmission data.
